stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वयि विहरणलोले बालजालैः प्रलम्ब-
-प्रमथनसविलम्बे धेनवः स्वैरचाराः ।
तृणकुतुकनिविष्टा दूरदूरं चरन्त्यः
किमपि विपिनमैषीकाख्यमीषाम्बभूवुः ॥ ५८-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna was engaged in playing with the gopas and in Pralambasura vadham.At that time, cows wandered deep in to the forest and reached another forest called Aishika.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvayi viharaṇalole bālajālaiḥ pralamba-
-pramathanasavilambe dhenavaḥ svairacārāḥ |
tṛṇakutukaniviṣṭā dūradūraṃ carantyaḥ
kimapi vipinamaiṣīkākhyamīṣāmbabhūvuḥ || 58-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अनधिगतनिदाघक्रौर्यबृन्दावनान्ता-
-द्बहिरिदमुपयाताः काननं धेनवस्ताः ।
तव विरहविषण्णा ऊष्मलग्रीष्मताप-
-प्रसरविसरदम्भस्याकुलाः स्तम्भमापुः ॥ ५८-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The Cows which have never been exposed to heat in Vrindavan, now experienced an intense heat in this forest. The separation from Krishna and the summer heat made them thirsty and motionless.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
anadhigatanidāghakrauryabṛndāvanāntā-
-dbahiridamupayātāḥ kānanaṃ dhenavastāḥ |
tava virahaviṣaṇṇā ūṣmalagrīṣmatāpa-
-prasaravisaradambhasyākulāḥ stambhamāpuḥ || 58-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
तदनु सह सहायैर्दूरमन्विष्य शौरे
गलितसरणिमुञ्जारण्यसञ्जातखेदम् ।
पशुकुलमभिवीक्ष्य क्षिप्रमानेतुमारा-
-त्त्वयि गतवति ही ही सर्वतोऽग्निर्जजृम्भे ॥ ५८-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna and gopas searched for the cows and reached the Munja forest. The Cows who lost their way were standing in distress. As Krishna went near them, a huge forest fire broke surrounding everyone faster.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tadanu saha sahāyairdūramanviṣya śaure
galitasaraṇimuñjāraṇyasañjātakhedam |
paśukulamabhivīkṣya kṣipramānetumārā-
-ttvayi gatavati hī hī sarvato’gnirjajṛmbhe || 58-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
सकलहरिति दीप्ते घोरभाङ्कारभीमे
शिखिनि विहतमार्गा अर्धदग्धा इवार्ताः ।
अहह भुवनबन्धो पाहि पाहीति सर्वे
शरणमुपगतास्त्वां तापहर्तारमेकम् ॥ ५८-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The fire was blazing in all directions making huge sounds and obstructing every possible way to escape. The gopas and cows were tormented by the fire and felt as if they were half burnt. They took shelter in Krishna, the only friend and saviour of all sorrows and cried to Him to save them from the fire.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
sakalahariti dīpte ghorabhāṅkārabhīme
śikhini vihatamārgā ardhadagdhā ivārtāḥ |
ahaha bhuvanabandho pāhi pāhīti sarve
śaraṇamupagatāstvāṃ tāpahartāramekam || 58-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अलमलमतिभीत्य सर्वतो मीलयध्वं
दृशमिति तव वाचा मीलिताक्षेषु तेषु ।
क्व नु दवदहनोऽसौ कुत्र मुञ्जाटवी सा
सपदि ववृतिरे ते हन्त भाण्डीरदेशे ॥ ५८-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna asked the gopas to close their eyes and when they opened after some time, they were back in Bhaandeera forest under the same banyan tree.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
alamalamatibhītya sarvato mīlayadhvaṃ
dṛśamiti tava vācā mīlitākṣeṣu teṣu |
kva nu davadahano’sau kutra muñjāṭavī sā
sapadi vavṛtire te hanta bhāṇḍīradeśe || 58-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
जय जय तव माया केयमीशेति तेषां
नुतिभिरुदितहासो बद्धनानाविलासः ।
पुनरपि विपिनान्ते प्राचरः पाटलादि-
-प्रसवनिकरमात्रग्राह्यघर्मानुभावे ॥ ५८-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Gopas praised Krishna for his glory which He accepted with a gracious smile. Krishna continued to sport with the gopas making them happy in the forest blooming with Paatala flowers indicating it is summer season.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
jaya jaya tava māyā keyamīśeti teṣāṃ
nutibhiruditahāso baddhanānāvilāsaḥ |
punarapi vipinānte prācaraḥ pāṭalādi-
-prasavanikaramātragrāhyagharmānubhāve || 58-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वयि विमुखमिवोच्चैस्तापभारं वहन्तं
तव भजनवदन्तः पङ्कमुच्छोषयन्तम् ।
तव भुजवदुदञ्चद्भूरितेजःप्रवाहं
तपसमयमनैषीर्यामुनेषु स्थलेषु ॥ ५८-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The intense heat of the summer time was like the weight of the heat of grief carried by people in their minds who are indifferent to Bhagwan. It was also like the heat which is created by worshipping Bhagwan, which dries up all the mud and slush of devotees. It was like the brilliance flowing from the chakra in Krishna’s hands. Krishna spent the rest of the summer season on the banks of Yamuna.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvayi vimukhamivoccaistāpabhāraṃ vahantaṃ
tava bhajanavadantaḥ paṅkamucchoṣayantam |
tava bhujavadudañcadbhūritejaḥpravāhaṃ
tapasamayamanaiṣīryāmuneṣu sthaleṣu || 58-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
तदनु जलदजालैस्त्वद्वपुस्तुल्यभाभि-
-र्विकसदमलविद्युत्पीतवासोविलासैः ।
सकलभुवनभाजां हर्षदां वर्षवेलां
क्षितिधरकुहरेषु स्वैरवासी व्यनैषीः ॥ ५८-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The rainy season came where in the clouds resembled Krishna's body and the lightening was like His beautiful yellow garment. Krishna along with the gopas and cows spent the rainy season in the caves of the mountain Govardhana very happily.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tadanu jaladajālaistvadvapustulyabhābhi-
-rvikasadamalavidyutpītavāsovilāsaiḥ |
sakalabhuvanabhājāṃ harṣadāṃ varṣavelāṃ
kṣitidharakuhareṣu svairavāsī vyanaiṣīḥ || 58-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
कुहरतलनिविष्टं त्वां गरिष्ठं गिरीन्द्रः
शिखिकुलनवकेकाकाकुभिः स्तोत्रकारी ।
स्फुटकुटजकदम्बस्तोमपुष्पाञ्जलिं च
प्रविदधदनुभेजे देव गोवर्धनोऽसौ ॥ ५८-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The mountain king Govardhana extended its hospitality by singing hymns of praise to Krishna, in the form of cooings of peacocks. The mountain worshipped Krishna by offering bloomed Jasmine and Kadamba flowers which fell from branches at His feet.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kuharatalaniviṣṭaṃ tvāṃ gariṣṭhaṃ girīndraḥ
śikhikulanavakekākākubhiḥ stotrakārī |
sphuṭakuṭajakadambastomapuṣpāñjaliṃ ca
pravidadhadanubheje deva govardhano’sau || 58-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अथ शरदमुपेतां तां भवद्भक्तचेतो-
-विमलसलिलपूरां मानयन् काननेषु ।
तृणममलवनान्ते चारु सञ्चारयन् गाः
पवनपुरपते त्वं देहि मे देहसौख्यम् ॥ ५८-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Then the spring season arrived with streams full of pure water, like the pure minds of Krishna’s devotees. Krishna enjoyed the spring season allowing the cows to graze in the fertile grasslands. Bhattathiri prayed to Lord Guruvayoorappan to cure him of his afflictions and bless with good health.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
atha śaradamupetāṃ tāṃ bhavadbhaktaceto-
-vimalasalilapūrāṃ mānayan kānaneṣu |
tṛṇamamalavanānte cāru sañcārayan gāḥ
pavanapurapate tvaṃ dehi me dehasaukhyam || 58-10 ||
